_how_to_use: COPY this file, rename it (e.g. y11-ionic-bonding.json), fill it in,
then add one entry to index.json (copy an existing entry, change
quizId, title, yearLevel and file). That is the whole process.
Any key starting with an underscore is a comment — the app ignores
them, so you can delete them or leave them in.
_quizId: Unique id for this quiz. kebab-case (lowercase-with-hyphens). Must EXACTLY match the quizId you put in index.json.
_title: Shown to students at the top of the quiz.
title: Example Topic
_subtitle: Optional. Small text under the title, e.g. 'After-lab quiz'. Delete the line if not needed.
subtitle: After-lab quiz
_yearLevel: Used to filter the quiz list. Keep the wording consistent ('Year 9', 'Year 11').
_durationMinutes: Optional. Shows students an expected time and a countdown. The countdown NEVER submits or locks anything.
_classCodes: The classes that will sit this quiz. Students pick one from a dropdown.
_intro: Optional. A sentence or two on the start screen.
intro: Answer from what you saw in the lab. This is a self-check, not a test.
_questions: Each question needs: a unique id, the stem (question text), and 2 to 6 options. EXACTLY ONE option has "correct": true. EVERY option needs a "why" — this is the whole point of the app: students see why their wrong answer was wrong AND why the right one is right. Write the whys like you would explain it to the student across the desk.

questions._misconception: Optional. ONLY the teacher dashboard shows this. Note what choosing a wrong answer here usually reveals about a student's thinking.
questions.misconception: Students who get this wrong usually think X instead of Y.

options.why: Explain WHY this is correct — the reasoning, not just 'this is right'.
Explain the specific mistake a student makes when they pick this.
Every option needs its own why — the app refuses to load the quiz if one is missing.

questions.stem: Second question — ids must be unique (q1, q2, q3…)?
